trial_court: Principal Family Court, Madras, H.M.O.P.1007 of 1988
facts_of_case: The husband and wife got married in 1987 but the marriage was not consummated. The wife's father sent a false horoscope to the husband seeking alliance for his daughter. The husband discovered the truth and the wife's family apologized for the fraud.

legal_principles.principle: Consent obtained prior to the date of marriage cannot be considered fraudulent if the correct information was disclosed.
legal_principles.held: In view of the specific pleadings in the counter affidavit, which has not been denied by way of filing a reply by the husband, as well as the oral evidence of the wife that the appellant was aware of the correct date of birth as 6-1-1961 prior to the date of marriage, i.e., on 8-3-87, it is not open to the appellant to contend that his consent was obtained fraudulently.
cited_cases: A. Premchand vs V. Padmapriya on 1 November, 1996

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party alleging fraud to prove it.
legal_principles.held: It is not open to the appellant to contend that his consent was obtained fraudulently.

outcome.final_order: The trial court's dismissal of the petition for nullity was set aside and the marriage was annulled.

use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for nullity of marriage
advising on Hindu Marriage Act implications
